title: Catalog: n = p + 2^k (de Polignac / Romanoff / Erdős)
connection: n = p + 2^k (de Polignac / Romanoff / Erdős) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ Σ_k 1/log n ≍ O(1) (log n terms each 1/log n). Obstruction: covering congruences {0 mod 2, 0 mod 3, 1 mod 4, 3 mod 8, 7 mod 12, 23 mod 24} force n−2^k divisible by a small prime. Status: false infinitely often (an AP of odd failures, Erdős 1950); Romanoff: positive lower density of representables. Mechanism: failure = periodic orbit k ↦ 2^k mod m covered by finitely many moduli; density = Romanoff's L¹ bound on r(n).
why: Canonical O(1)-count failure; ES has no periodic witness parameter, so the covering mechanism has no direct ES analogue — the reason why should be stated as a lemma.
first_step: Write the ES witness set at p as orbit(s) of a map and test whether any finite modulus set can 'cover' it; check whether this reproduces B1 sterility.

title: Catalog: n = p + 2^a + 2^b (Crocker)
connection: n = p + 2^a + 2^b (Crocker) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ log n. Obstruction: no single-modulus covering; failures come from an explicit sparse family. Status: false infinitely often (Crocker 1971; Pan 2011 gives ≫ x^{1−ε} odd exceptions ≤ x). Mechanism: an explicit sparse family of odd n (check whether it is built from 2^{2^m}−1 and Fermat-number divisibility, as commonly described).
why: Log-count, no covering, still false i.o. — the sharpest warning that 'log² count + no local obstruction' is not enough; ES's count is log² p.
first_step: Read Crocker 1971 (Pacific J. Math.) and isolate the exact structural input; ask whether an ES analogue (p tied to 2^{2^m}) exists among primes.

title: Catalog: odd n = p + 2^a + 2^b + 2^c (Sun's conjecture: every odd n > 8)
connection: odd n = p + 2^a + 2^b + 2^c (Sun's conjecture: every odd n > 8) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ log² n — same order as ES. Obstruction: none known. Status: open (conjectured by Z.-W. Sun, arXiv:0901.3075). Mechanism: none; numerics only.
why: Exact twin of ES in expected count (log²) with additive instead of multiplicative witnesses; any proof or disproof calibrates ES directly.
first_step: Check whether Crocker's construction extends to three powers (search 'p+2^a+2^b+2^c exceptions'); compute min witness count / log² n up to 10^9.
refs: arXiv:0901.3075 (Sun, Mixed sums of primes and other terms)

title: Catalog: Sierpiński numbers k·2^n + 1 (78557)
connection: Sierpiński numbers k·2^n + 1 (78557) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ Σ_n 1/(n log 2) = ∞ (divergent, log N up to N) but along a periodic orbit. Obstruction: covering set {3,5,7,13,19,37,73}. Status: false for specific k (covering); smallest Sierpiński number still open (78557 conjectured). Mechanism: covering system on n; also partial algebraic factorisation variants (Filaseta et al.).
why: Shows a divergent expected count can still vanish identically when the parameter is periodic mod the covering moduli.
first_step: Formulate an 'ES-Sierpiński' question: a family p(t) of primes candidates for which every ES certificate line is killed mod fixed primes; relate to T1.

title: Catalog: Riesel numbers k·2^n − 1 (509203)
connection: Riesel numbers k·2^n − 1 (509203) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: divergent log, periodic parameter. Obstruction: covering. Status: false for specific k; minimality open. Mechanism: covering.
why: Same mechanism as Sierpiński; included for completeness of the covering family.
first_step: Note: ES certificate families are also 'k·m + 1' shapes (4Cp+1): check whether any covering-type identity is impossible for them by B1.

title: Catalog: Brier numbers (both Sierpiński and Riesel)
connection: Brier numbers (both Sierpiński and Riesel) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: divergent log. Obstruction: simultaneous coverings. Status: exist (explicit large k). Mechanism: two coverings.
why: Simultaneous covering of two linear families is possible — relevant if ES were reduced to two simultaneous divisor conditions.
first_step: Check the size of the smallest known Brier number and the covering moduli used.

title: Catalog: n − 2^k composite for all k (Erdős; e.g. via covering)
connection: n − 2^k composite for all k (Erdős; e.g. via covering) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: O(1). Obstruction: covering. Status: infinitely many such odd n. Mechanism: covering.
why: Dual phrasing of the p + 2^k problem; witness = prime value of a shifted sparse sequence.
first_step: Compare: ES at p asks for a divisor in a class of a p-shifted thin sequence (4Cp+1, C varying) — not a prime value; note the difference in kind.

title: Catalog: n = p + F_k (prime + Fibonacci number)
connection: n = p + F_k (prime + Fibonacci number) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: O(1). Obstruction: covering congruences on the Fibonacci orbit (periodic mod m, Pisano period). Status: check whether: positive proportion represented and an AP of failures known (Wu–Sun style). Mechanism: Pisano periodicity makes covering possible.
why: Any linear-recurrence witness sequence is periodic mod m, enabling coverings; ES witnesses are divisor-type, not recurrence-type.
first_step: Search 'sum of a prime and a Fibonacci number covering' to confirm the AP-of-failures result.

title: Catalog: Romanoff density for p + 2^k (lower density)
connection: Romanoff density for p + 2^k (lower density) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: O(1). Obstruction: partial covering. Status: positive lower density proved; upper density < 1/2 (van der Corput / Erdős). Mechanism: Cauchy–Schwarz + sieve upper bound for r(n) second moment.
why: Example where second-moment + positive mean gives positive density but not 'almost all'; ES has almost-all, a stronger regime.
first_step: Compute the analogue of Romanoff's second moment Σ R(p)² for ES (count ≍ log² p): already known? compare to Elsholtz–Tao.

title: Catalog: p + 2k² for odd composite n (Goldbach's other conjecture)
connection: p + 2k² for odd composite n (Goldbach's other conjecture) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ √n / log n (power). Obstruction: none local. Status: false: 5777 and 5993 (Stern 1856); no others known, finitely many expected. Mechanism: small-n fluctuation with power count.
why: Calibrates sporadic small failures (like U(n)'s sporadic list) under a power count: failures happen only at very small n.
first_step: Fit failure probability vs n for p + 2k² and compare with ES's sporadic structures (U(n) list) on a log-count scale.

title: Catalog: Goldbach binary: 2n = p + q
connection: Goldbach binary: 2n = p + q ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ n / log² n (power). Obstruction: none (parity barrier for sieves). Status: open; almost all (Chudakov, van der Corput, Estermann 1938); verified to 4·10^18. Mechanism: circle method for almost all; parity problem blocks pointwise.
why: Power count yet open: shows count size alone never suffices; ES is far thinner but has multiplicative (divisor) structure.
first_step: Contrast the exceptional-set exponents: Goldbach exceptions ≪ x^{1−δ} vs ES exceptions ≪ x·exp(−c log^{2/3} x); ask why ES's is weaker.

title: Catalog: Ternary Goldbach (Helfgott)
connection: Ternary Goldbach (Helfgott) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ n² / log³ n. Obstruction: parity only. Status: proved for all odd n > 5. Mechanism: circle method + explicit computation.
why: Prototype of (T): thick reservoir + exact extraction; ES lacks a power reservoir.
first_step: None beyond noting it as the (T) anchor.

title: Catalog: Linnik–Gallagher: 2n = p + q + 2^{k_1}+…+2^{k_K}
connection: Linnik–Gallagher: 2n = p + q + 2^{k_1}+…+2^{k_K} ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: power (Goldbach part) × polylog. Obstruction: none. Status: proved for K ≥ 13 (Heath-Brown–Puchta), K ≥ 6 claimed (Li–Liu 2610.15784). Mechanism: Goldbach reservoir absorbs polylog factor.
why: Shows exactly how polylog witnesses ride on power reservoirs; ES has no reservoir.
first_step: None (well covered in repo).

title: Catalog: n = p + m² (Hardy–Littlewood Conjecture H)
connection: n = p + m² (Hardy–Littlewood Conjecture H) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ √n/log n × singular series. Obstruction: algebraic: n = square has m² − k² = (m−k)(m+k) factorisation — fails at squares. Status: open for non-squares; almost-all results known; squares are the forced exceptions. Mechanism: factorisation identity at squares (a 'T1-like' algebraic obstruction).
why: Exact structural analogue of ES's T1: squares are excluded by an algebraic identity, everything else expected. ES's square obstruction is reciprocity-type, but the shape matches.
first_step: Write the ES T1 obstruction in the same language: does 4/m² have a 'difference of squares' factorisation forcing certificate lines empty?

title: Catalog: Lemoine–Levy: odd n = p + 2q
connection: Lemoine–Levy: odd n = p + 2q ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ n / log² n. Obstruction: none. Status: open; verified numerically. Mechanism: circle method for almost all.
why: Goldbach-type control item.
first_step: None.

title: Catalog: Chen: 2n = p + P₂
connection: Chen: 2n = p + P₂ ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: power. Obstruction: none. Status: proved for large n. Mechanism: sieve with switching + Bombieri–Vinogradov.
why: Sieve beating parity by accepting a weaker witness — ES analogue would be accepting x,y,z with a weaker property.
first_step: Define an 'ES-almost' witness (e.g. 4/p = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z + ε with ε a controlled unit fraction of huge denominator) and see if sieve gives it.

title: Catalog: Linnik: n = p + x² + y²
connection: Linnik: n = p + x² + y² ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ n / log n. Obstruction: none. Status: proved (Linnik dispersion; Hooley under GRH first). Mechanism: dispersion method.
why: Mixed multiplicative/quadratic problem proved pointwise thanks to power reservoir.
first_step: None.

title: Catalog: Every large n = p + squarefree (Estermann)
connection: Every large n = p + squarefree (Estermann) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: power. Obstruction: none. Status: proved. Mechanism: elementary sieve.
why: Control.
first_step: None.

title: Catalog: Prime in (n², (n+1)²) (Legendre)
connection: Prime in (n², (n+1)²) (Legendre) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ n / log n. Obstruction: none. Status: open; known for (x, x + x^{0.525}). Mechanism: zero-density.
why: Short-interval existence with power count still open; calibrates ES's lack of averaging.
first_step: None.

title: Catalog: Bertrand: prime in (n, 2n)
connection: Bertrand: prime in (n, 2n) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ n/log n. Obstruction: none. Status: proved for all n. Mechanism: elementary binomial-coefficient divisibility (Chebyshev/Erdős).
why: Pointwise existence from an explicit integer (C(2n,n)) whose factorisation is forced — a 'thick deterministic object' with exact extraction.
first_step: Look for an explicit p-tied integer (like C(2n,n)) whose prime factorisation provably contains a divisor in the ES class −1 mod 4C.

title: Catalog: Least prime ≡ a mod q (Linnik)
connection: Least prime ≡ a mod q (Linnik) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ q^{...}; window x with count x/(φ(q)log x). Obstruction: none. Status: proved P(a,q) ≪ q^5 (Xylouris). Mechanism: log-free zero density + Deuring–Heilbronn.
why: Fixed-modulus character event; ES's moduli move with the witness (B2).
first_step: None (seen).

title: Catalog: Least quadratic non-residue n(p)
connection: Least quadratic non-residue n(p) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: polylog window under GRH. Obstruction: none. Status: proved ≪ p^{1/(4√e)+ε} (Burgess); ≤ 2 log² p under GRH (Bach). Mechanism: character sums / L-function zeros.
why: ES sign layer is a least-QNR event (repo F6); the class layer is not.
first_step: None (seen).

title: Catalog: Artin's primitive root conjecture
connection: Artin's primitive root conjecture ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: positive density of primes; for each a an infinite set. Obstruction: a = square or −1 excluded (local/algebraic). Status: conditional on GRH (Hooley 1967); unconditionally one of any three suitable a works (Heath-Brown 1986). Mechanism: Chebotarev in Kummer extensions; Heath-Brown via Fouvry–Iwaniec + sieve.
why: Heath-Brown's 'at most two exceptions' is a rigidity-of-exceptions theorem: ES might admit a 'one of a few certificate families works' statement.
first_step: Try: prove that for every p at least one of three named ES certificate families works, using Heath-Brown's style of multiplicative-relations argument.

title: Catalog: Primitive roots: existence of a primitive root mod every prime
connection: Primitive roots: existence of a primitive root mod every prime ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: φ(p−1) ≥ 1. Obstruction: none. Status: proved. Mechanism: group structure (cyclicity of F_p^×).
why: Existence from algebraic structure with count φ(p−1) — (R) with a thick count.
first_step: None.

title: Catalog: Fermat: p ≡ 1 mod 4 ⇒ p = x² + y²
connection: Fermat: p ≡ 1 mod 4 ⇒ p = x² + y² ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: exactly 1 (up to signs/order). Obstruction: local (p ≡ 3 mod 4 fails). Status: proved for all p (many proofs: Euler descent, Thue lemma, Gaussian integers, Zagier involution, continued fractions). Mechanism: (R): parity of fixed points of an involution; pigeonhole (Thue); UFD.
why: O(1) count, pointwise, same prime class as ES's hard case — the strongest positive anchor. ES lacks a known involution with odd fixed-point count.
first_step: Compute R(p) mod 2 (ordered and unordered ES counts) for p ≡ 1 mod 24 up to 10^6 to test for a parity law (see INVOLUTION_ES.md).

title: Catalog: p = x² + 2y² (p ≡ 1,3 mod 8), x² + 3y², x² + 7y²…
connection: p = x² + 2y² (p ≡ 1,3 mod 8), x² + 3y², x² + 7y²… ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: O(1). Obstruction: local (class mod 8, 3, 7). Status: proved. Mechanism: class number one / genus theory.
why: O(1) count pointwise from h = 1: the class group being trivial forces representation.
first_step: Ask whether ES certificates at p are parametrised by a 'class group' whose triviality would force ES; compare QUATERNION_ES.md.

title: Catalog: p = x² + 27y² ⟺ 2 is a cubic residue mod p (p ≡ 1 mod 3)
connection: p = x² + 27y² ⟺ 2 is a cubic residue mod p (p ≡ 1 mod 3) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: O(1). Obstruction: reciprocity (cubic). Status: proved. Mechanism: class field theory (ring class field).
why: Pointwise criteria via class field theory carry reciprocity conditions; ES's T1 is reciprocity-type too.
first_step: Look for a ring class field whose splitting of p controls existence of an ES certificate of a fixed shape.
refs: Cox, Primes of the form x²+ny²

title: Catalog: p = x² + 64y² ⟺ 2 is a quartic residue (p ≡ 1 mod 8)
connection: p = x² + 64y² ⟺ 2 is a quartic residue (p ≡ 1 mod 8) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: O(1). Obstruction: quartic reciprocity. Status: proved (Gauss). Mechanism: biquadratic reciprocity.
why: Quartic residue symbols separate primes into 'yes/no' classes pointwise; ES survives all such splittings (no BM), but certificate families might each be governed by such symbols.
first_step: Tabulate for each fixed ES certificate shape the governing residue symbol (quadratic/quartic) and check whether some finite set of shapes covers all symbol patterns.

title: Catalog: Negative Pell x² − py² = −1 for primes p ≡ 1 mod 4 (Legendre)
connection: Negative Pell x² − py² = −1 for primes p ≡ 1 mod 4 (Legendre) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: 1 fundamental solution. Obstruction: local: fails if a prime ≡ 3 mod 4 divides d. Status: proved for all primes p ≡ 1 mod 4. Mechanism: parity descent on the fundamental unit of x² − py² = 1.
why: Pointwise O(1) existence at exactly ES's hard primes, proved by elementary descent on a forced object (the fundamental unit). ES lacks a 'forced object'.
first_step: Try a Legendre-style descent: start from the fundamental unit ε_p of Q(√p) (or a forced ES-adjacent object) and case-split on gcds to produce a certificate.

title: Catalog: Negative Pell for general d (Stevenhagen conjecture)
connection: Negative Pell for general d (Stevenhagen conjecture) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: 1 or 0. Obstruction: local + 4-rank (Rédei). Status: Koymans–Pagano proved Stevenhagen's density. Mechanism: Rédei matrices, Smith's method.
why: Pointwise status governed by 2-power class group structure; density proved, pointwise only via governing fields.
first_step: Check whether ES solvability for p could be expressed via a Rédei-matrix-type invariant (cf. BRAINSTORM/bsB_redei_oddpart.md).

title: Catalog: Barrucand–Cohn: 8 | h(−4p) ⟺ p = x² + 32y²
connection: Barrucand–Cohn: 8 | h(−4p) ⟺ p = x² + 32y² ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: O(1). Obstruction: reciprocity. Status: proved. Mechanism: governing field Q(ζ8, ⁴√2)… / class field theory.
why: Pointwise criteria exist iff a governing field exists; 16-rank has none (Milovic/Koymans) yet density proved.
first_step: Ask: is there a 'governing field' for existence of ES certificates of bounded shape? If not, ES is in the 16-rank regime (density only).

title: Catalog: 16-rank of Q(√−2p) (Koymans–Milovic)
connection: 16-rank of Q(√−2p) (Koymans–Milovic) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: O(1) indicator. Obstruction: no governing field. Status: density proved (Vinogradov-type sums). Mechanism: bilinear sums over Gaussian primes.
why: Example: no pointwise criterion, only density, due to lack of governing field — strong ES analogue.
first_step: Read Koymans–Milovic's bilinear sum and check whether ES's E1 event can be written as a 'spin' with similar oscillation.

title: Catalog: Sums of three squares (Legendre–Gauss)
connection: Sums of three squares (Legendre–Gauss) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ √n L(1,χ) (class number). Obstruction: local: 4^a(8b+7). Status: proved. Mechanism: genus theory + class number > 0.
why: Power count; pointwise thanks to class-number positivity (R). See THREE_SQUARES.md.
first_step: None (seen).

title: Catalog: Ramanujan's x² + y² + 10z² representing odd n
connection: Ramanujan's x² + y² + 10z² representing odd n ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ √n. Obstruction: spinor/genus subtleties; 18 known exceptions. Status: finite exception list proved under GRH (Ono–Soundararajan 1997); unconditionally ineffective. Mechanism: Siegel ineffectivity / GRH for L-functions of weight-3/2 forms.
why: Model of 'finite sporadic exceptions + ineffective' — like U(n). ES's sporadic list for U(n) might be finite only via an ineffective argument.
first_step: Compare the U(n) sporadic list {105, 2961, 3985, 25305, 111969, 978145} to Ramanujan-form exceptions: any common prime-factor pattern?

title: Catalog: Ternary forms, large n in a spinor genus (Duke–Schulze-Pillot)
connection: Ternary forms, large n in a spinor genus (Duke–Schulze-Pillot) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ n^{1/2−ε}. Obstruction: spinor exceptions t·m². Status: proved for n ≫ 1 ineffectively. Mechanism: Iwaniec's bound for half-integral weight Fourier coefficients.
why: Spinor exceptional square classes are the closest classical analogue of ES's 'odd squares' obstruction.
first_step: Check whether T1 can be read as a spinor-exception phenomenon for an attached ternary quadratic form (QUATERNION_ES.md).

title: Catalog: Ternary positive forms with spinor exceptions (Schulze-Pillot, Kneser)
connection: Ternary positive forms with spinor exceptions (Schulze-Pillot, Kneser) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: power. Obstruction: square classes t·m². Status: fully classified for which square classes fail. Mechanism: spinor norm / quadratic reciprocity.
why: Square-class obstructions come from spinor norms: the theory explains exactly which squares fail.
first_step: Look up whether a 'spinor norm' type invariant can be attached to the ES variety restricted to n = m².

title: Catalog: Bhargava–Hanke 290 theorem / Conway–Schneeberger 15
connection: Bhargava–Hanke 290 theorem / Conway–Schneeberger 15 ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: power. Obstruction: local. Status: proved: universal iff represents 1..290. Mechanism: escalation + modular forms (Eisenstein vs cusp bounds) for each escalator.
why: Finite certificate theorem: verifying small n suffices. ES has none (U(n) sporadic).
first_step: Ask whether there is an ES 'escalation' statement: if all primes up to B have certificates of some shape then all do? (likely false; record why).

title: Catalog: Rouse 451 theorem (forms representing all odd n)
connection: Rouse 451 theorem (forms representing all odd n) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: power. Obstruction: local. Status: proved conditional on three ternary forms representing all odd numbers. Mechanism: escalation + modular forms.

title: Catalog: Lagrange four squares
connection: Lagrange four squares ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ σ(n). Obstruction: none. Status: proved. Mechanism: identity/composition (Euler four-square) + descent.

connection: Sun's 1-3-5 conjecture (n = x²+y²+z²+w² with x+3y+5z a square) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: power (≈ √n). Obstruction: none. Status: proved (Machiavelo–Tsopanidis 2021). Mechanism: quaternion (Lipschitz) arithmetic, factorization.

connection: Gauss Eureka: n = three triangular numbers ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ √n. Obstruction: none. Status: proved. Mechanism: three squares for 8n+3.

connection: Pollock tetrahedral-number conjecture (≤ 5 tetrahedrals) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ n^{2/3}. Obstruction: none. Status: open (verified numerically). Mechanism: none.

connection: Waring: g(k), G(k) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: power. Obstruction: local for small. Status: g(k) known except finitely many k; G(k) bounds. Mechanism: circle method + Vinogradov.

connection: Sums of three cubes x³+y³+z³ = k ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: solutions up to height H ≍ log H (grows slowly). connection: Sums of four signed cubes (n ≢ ±4 mod 9: Demjanenko) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: infinite families. Obstruction: none for those classes. Status: proved for n ≢ ±4 mod 9. Mechanism: polynomial identities covering residue classes + quadratic forms.

connection: Five signed cubes: 6x = (x+1)³ + (x−1)³ − 2x³ ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: infinite. Obstruction: none. Status: proved for all n. Mechanism: polynomial identity.

title: Catalog: Markoff-type integral Hasse x²+y²+z²−xyz = k
connection: Markoff-type integral Hasse x²+y²+z²−xyz = k ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: few orbits; count of points of height ≤ H ≍ (log H)^2. Obstruction: integral Brauer–Manin explains some failures. Status: Hasse fails for infinitely many k (Ghosh–Sarnak); BM explains a positive proportion (Loughran–Mitankin, Colliot-Thélène–Wei–Xu); not all failures BM. Mechanism: reduction theory for the Vieta group action: fundamental domain search shows emptiness.
why: Same 'integral points on affine cubic surface' type as ES, with infinitely many non-BM Hasse failures — direct evidence that no-BM does not imply existence.
first_step: Check whether ES's affine cubic surface admits a Vieta-type reduction (fundamental domain) — compare MARKOFF_ES.md.

connection: Markoff mod p: transitivity of the Vieta group on X*(p) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ p² points. Obstruction: none. Status: proved for all but finitely many p (Bourgain–Gamburd–Sarnak + W. Chen 2024). Mechanism: Chen: every orbit size ≡ 0 mod p (divisibility invariant).
why: Divisibility invariant on orbit sizes forcing a single orbit: ES lacks an infinite group action.
first_step: Search for any nontrivial correspondence/group acting on ES solutions mod p (beyond permutations); see UNIT_ORBIT_ES.md.
